global_estimate.method: Each disclosed level is projected to the as-of date on that company’s own dated trend (rolled forward daily); components without a trend are held or estimated with stated ranges. Router traffic (OpenRouter) is excluded to avoid double counting hosts and labs. Logical tokens include cached input. Low = latest levels held flat or the low estimate; high = trend ×1.25 or the high estimate. This is an estimate, not a disclosure.

spend.note: Tokens × each vendor’s realized list price per million logical tokens on OpenRouter (last 30 days, cache reads included; OpenAI excludes open-weight gpt-oss). Consumer and subscription tokens are valued at API prices, not billed. Calibration: OpenAI’s ~$50B revenue run-rate with an assumed 25–30% API share implies $33–41M/day, about 1.6–2× this API estimate. DeepInfra’s >$100M ARR is consistent with an understatement, but it also includes image models, embeddings and GPU rental, so it is not a clean token check. Treat spend as a lower bound.

Anthropic.basis: Q3 consumption revenue ÷ $0.80 per million logical tokens (OpenRouter-measured Claude mix at list prices), projected to the as-of date on its revenue trend. Cloud marketplaces: Anthropic recognizes CSP-marketplace sales gross; 44% of January–September revenue ($33.2B) is ≈$14.6B, or ≈67T/day through Bedrock, Vertex AI and Foundry combined at ≈$0.80/Mtok (January–September average), ≈56% of consumption-billed traffic if those sales are all consumption. This is inside the Anthropic estimate, not additional; no cloud reports Anthropic-only tokens, and Bedrock’s 17× growth has no absolute baseline.

xAI / Grok.basis: API plus consumer text; OpenRouter floor ≈74B/day; see the Grok estimate note

OpenAI has not said whether its tokens/min counts cached input; Anthropic’s estimate includes ~80% cache reads, so the like-for-like gap may be smaller.

spacex_2027.note: CEO on the Q3 2026 call (Oct 20): "an incremental 10 gigawatts… in 2027… So 13 total" (cumulative nameplate compute, ≈IT power; spoken target, grade B). Filed nameplate 1.7 GW at Sep 30 2026 (10-Q, A); CFO: nearly 2.2 GW by end-October, 2.5–3 GW at year-end 2026. Epoch tracks three SpaceX sites (Colossus 1, Colossus 2 Tulane Rd, QTS Atlanta) and none of Macroharder, Minihard, Gun Range, Spam, Starbase or TeraFab; its facility-power PUE is ≈1.25–1.35. SemiAnalysis (Nov 3) reports 3.6 GW under construction (analyst estimate).
spacex_2027.basis: nameplate (≈IT power: GPUs × all-in GPU power, excluding cooling and facility overhead)

Subscription traffic is not in the token count, so this overstates cost per token; Anthropic’s models are also likely heavier than the market average.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Colette Kress, EVP & CFO
capacity_quotes.quote: Although we will work to close the supply-demand gap, we expect supply to remain a bottleneck at least through the end of fiscal year 2028.
capacity_quotes.context: Q2 FY27 call (NVIDIA IR-hosted FactSet transcript). Kress called the ~70% FY28 growth guide 'a supply-constrained outlook'; Huang said 'our demand is much greater than 70%'.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Amy Hood, CFO
capacity_quotes.quote: Customer demand continues to exceed available supply.
capacity_quotes.context: FY27 Q1 guidance: Azure +49-50% cc despite 3P GPU-as-a-service contracts slipping to H2; Q1 capex $45.2B, below plan on delayed 3P deliveries. Transcript linked from microsoft.com/en-us/investor.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Michael Intrator, Co-founder, Chairman & CEO
capacity_quotes.quote: Our near-term capacity remains effectively sold out.
capacity_quotes.context: Q2 2026 call (Motley Fool transcript syndicated on Webull; CoreWeave IR site returned 403). Same call: 'We expect demand to meaningfully exceed supply for years.' Q3 call is Nov 10, not yet held.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Form S-1/A (company filing)
capacity_quotes.quote: We have historically operated in a compute-constrained environment in which demand for compute has exceeded the supply available to us.
capacity_quotes.context: IPO risk factors. Also says it has 'in the past sought quantities of compute from CSPs in excess of what those partners were willing to provide.'

capacity_quotes.speaker: Form S-1/A (company filing, MD&A)
capacity_quotes.quote: When customer demand or research needs exceed this long-term capacity, we procure short-term compute that currently costs significantly more than comparable compute procured under our multi-year commitments.
capacity_quotes.context: Q3 2026 included $5.0B of short-term compute, cutting adjusted operating margin from 19% to 15%; it expects short-term compute use to keep rising near term.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Q2 2026 shareholder letter (Arkady Volozh, Founder & CEO)
capacity_quotes.quote: We could sell our entire 2027 capacity on these terms today. We are deliberately not doing so because we see higher value in retaining some capacity for immediate customer needs.
capacity_quotes.context: Letter filed as 6-K Ex. 99.2. It also calls prepayment 'the market standard for securing capacity in a supply-constrained environment.' Q3 results are due Nov 12, not yet out.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Andy Jassy, President & CEO
capacity_quotes.quote: We're installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds, and almost as fast as we install capacity, customers are gobbling it up.
capacity_quotes.context: Q3 2026 call, AWS +39.3%. Backlog $578B, 'growing triple digits'; short-term prior-gen Trainium capacity now sells 'at a premium compared to the first half of the year.'

capacity_quotes.speaker: Susan Li, CFO
capacity_quotes.quote: overall the landscape for compute, remains pretty constrained and that's certainly something that we are experiencing ourselves.
capacity_quotes.context: Q3 2026 follow-up call (Meta IR PDF). She added Meta is 'facing the same kinds of capacity constraints as everyone else'; Zuckerberg said Muse isn't global yet because it is compute-intensive.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP & CFO
capacity_quotes.quote: given the supply constrained environment, we started utilizing third-party compute capacity at the end of Q3 and will ramp usage in Q4.
capacity_quotes.context: Q3 2026 call (Motley Fool transcript; abc.xyz returned 403). Flagged near-term Cloud margin headwinds. Kurian: 'we could obviously serve a lot more demand with capacity.'

capacity_quotes.speaker: Q1 FY27 earnings release (company statement)
capacity_quotes.quote: Customer demand for AI Cloud Training and Inferencing Services continues to grow faster than supply.
capacity_quotes.context: 8-K Ex. 99.1: RPO at $664B, >300k GPUs delivered. On the call, CEO Clay Magouyrk cited 97.9% GPU utilization and renewals or resales at a 20% premium (per Motley Fool transcript).

capacity_quotes.speaker: Yang Gao, Data Analyst
capacity_quotes.quote: Hyperscaler H100 rates fell in every region, but at very different speeds
capacity_quotes.context: Prior-gen pricing softening at hyperscalers: H100 rates fell ~26-54% from Q1 2025 to Q3 2026. Neocloud H100 rates have recovered since early 2026, so this is mixed rather than a glut.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Susan Li, CFO (CFO Outlook Commentary)
capacity_quotes.quote: Our current capacity and what is scheduled to come online gives us the flexibility to allocate resources across model training, core business growth, and the development and support of new products.
capacity_quotes.context: Q3 2026 press release (8-K Ex. 99.1). Signals comfort with planned supply, and 2026 capex was narrowed to $135-145B. Contrast with her 'pretty constrained' remark on the same day.

capacity_quotes.speaker: Andy Jassy, President & CEO
capacity_quotes.quote: they will have plenty of capacity to be able to use in AWS
capacity_quotes.context: Q3 2026 Q&A reassurance that AWS keeps on-demand capacity for EC2/Bedrock. He also said gigawatt-scale blocks are reserved well in advance, into 2027-2029.

neocloud_risk.note: Latest filings, with debt filed after each period added pro forma (Nov 4 fact-check), with Q3 2026 results for Cipher, Core Scientific, Hut 8, IREN and TeraWulf (filed Nov 2–6); others still on Q2 until they file. Cloud backlog (RPO) runs 2–7 years; landlord contracted rent runs 10–20 years, so debt ÷ annual contracted revenue is the fairer comparison than backlog ÷ debt.
